doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: Letting musicians go
summary: He rarely parts with bandmates unless someone is disruptive.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay. Thanks for answering that. Have you ever had to let someone go, a musician who made you angry about something?
Well or just, you know I’ve asked this question a number of times and I should say that most people say I’ve never fired anybody, I just don’t call them again.
Have you ever been in that position?

Certainly there are people that maybe you prefer to work with, so that will be the person you call for a job. Now if it’s someone that you’ve worked with over and over and over again, like say they’ve been in your band for years, and you decide to part ways then there has to be a really good reason. And really, the number one reason for that is simply if that person is becoming a problem if that person is disruptive. If that person is not contributing to the music because they’re constantly undermining maybe your decision
about something or just harping on about whatever comes to mind. A person like that can be a cancer in a band. I’ve never experienced that, fortunately.
